facts:
## CELL FACTS

Cell 火_正官 (Fire carrying The Magistrate). Persona The Magistrate (正官). Definition line: "Framework-mediated pressure, the standard that steadies". Keyword Order, charge gentle, poles catalyst Integrity / friction Rigidity. Family function: Order. Cost dimension: the standard that steadies; the frame that holds you holds you in. Arena: the gate, the seal, order, the appointed hour. Classical portrait: framework-mediated pressure; the standard that steadies; rank held by rules, rigidity as the shadow. Ruled domains: Career, Status, Order. Sibling (other polarity of the family): 七杀.
Element arena: Fire (flame, light, warmth, fuel, the hearth, the blaze). dm_element (which core reads this cell): Metal. structural_interaction seed: "Fire setting standard for Metal cross-polarity — the forge that refines and grants recognition".
- k2_overview: "Your Fire moves as the Magistrate: civic light, authority that illuminates. You carry rules the way lighthouses carry flame, visibly, warmly, for everyone’s navigation. People follow your lead because it brightens rather than binds. Office becomes you. Keep the light public and tended, and rank will keep arriving on its own."
- k2_functional: "You carry order like a lantern: visible standards others steer by, kept lit at personal cost."
- adj_chips: {"catalyst":["Upstanding","Squeaky-clean","Inspiring"],"friction":"[REDACTED: the words under test]"}
- k2_domain_readings: {"Career":"Your career runs on visible service: roles where leading and lighting are the same act. Teaching, governance, the public face of good systems. Seek podiums attached to substance.","Status":"Your standing is luminous and watched: warmth draws the credit and the scrutiny together. Live as if lit, because you are. The honest glow survives every inspection.","Order":"Your order is inspirational: people comply because you made the rule glow with purpose. That is rare governance. Write things down too. Light needs a lamp when you leave."}
- fn_reading.friction.ledger (three rows, index-aligned to adj_chips.friction; authored order is significance order):
  - row 0: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 1: [REDACTED: the target row]
  - row 2: [REDACTED: the target row]
- Sibling cell 火_七杀 chips (nothing you write may fit the sibling): {"catalyst":["Decisive","Daring","Crisis-ready"],"friction":["Too intense","Bossy","Burned-out"]}
- Sibling cell 火_七杀 friction row 0 drive passage, for the sibling test on the tension (this row must name a different either-or): "Your intensity marks people whether you mean it or not, and you usually do not. The heat that cuts through problems does not distinguish problems from bystanders, and the bystanders remember longer. You forget the flare by lunch. Nobody standing near it ever does."

Core element Metal, energy element Fire. Law: Fire tames Metal (火克金: the forge softens the blade). Relative to the core the energy is the tamer, so Fire is this core's Order. No chart is attached to this batch: the cell is written for every chart with a Metal core that shows Fire on the friction pole, so no percentage and no state of one chart appears in any value. The friction pole of Fire as the Order is the Underfueled band's case (the core burns more than it takes in); tone by pole: reminder. Rows: row 0, row 1, row 2, each with its three angles (drive, cost_self, cost_others: the drive, the cost to the reader, the cost to others; the app shows one angle per row by position rotation, so each passage must stand alone); one chip per row, written once and copied byte-identical onto the row's three fields. The pair cell 金_火's definition and advice for this pole are rewritten in the same batch (the pair skeleton) and are withheld here; no four-word run may be shared with them, so keep every phrase the ledger's own.

value.text: A rule you learned once stays in force long after it stops helping you. The rules that steady you also hold you in, so you keep the correct one ahead of the useful one. Remember you wrote most of these rules yourself, and you get to retire them.

value_b.text: You feel safer inside a rule than outside one, even a rule that stopped fitting. Fire sits in you beyond what your strength bears, so each new rule becomes one more to keep. Remember that you were meant to be steadied by the rules rather than kept by them.

value.text: Keeping to the rules is how you look after the people around you. Because one exception looks to you like a collapse starting, you give them the rule ahead of the one thing they asked for. Never forget that you hand the rules that hold you in to everyone living inside them with you.

value.text: The fear of slipping in public runs under most of what you do well. Since your standing is where you keep your worth, you would rather never be seen to slip than ever be at ease. Remember how much less you are watched for a slip than you are watching for one.

value_b.text: You live as if one slip would be the end of your standing. Because your status is where you keep your safety, you hide the slip ahead of fixing its cause. Remember that you have never once been as closely watched as you are afraid of being.

value.text: In public, one slip stays with you longer than with anyone who saw it. Afraid to slip, you put looking steady ahead of feeling rested, so a good day tires you as much as a bad one. Remind yourself how much ease you never allow yourself for slips you never even made.

value.text: Saying yes to everyone is how you keep your place in their lives. Because a refused request feels like lost standing, you give everyone a small slice of you rather than anyone your whole self. You will want to remember that you give the people who need you most whatever is left over.
